title: Huhtamaki India Ltd - 509820 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Huhtamaki India Q2 CY26 net sales rose 23.1% to INR723 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.3%, with PBT up 77%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 net sales of INR723 crore, up about 23% YoY, with growth split roughly evenly across price, volume and product mix and broad-based across exports and domestic. EBITDA margin expanded to 10.5% from 8.3%, and PBT rose 77% to INR559 crore, with EPS up about 77%. H1 sales grew close to 12% and H1 EBIT margin was hit by a one-time INR8.8 crore prior-period depreciation charge; excluding it, EBIT margin was 7.6%. Management attributed the quarter to pricing pass-through of Middle East-driven raw material inflation, a healthy portfolio mix and productivity, plus some customer inventory build-up that it said would partly reverse.

financial_highlights.value: Growth of ~77.3% YoY (absolute value not stated)

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports grew at roughly the same rate as domestic in Q2; exports are about 30% of sales volume. Management said duty-related challenges are stabilising.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic growth was almost identical to exports at about 23%; volume growth in liquid and home care categories was highlighted.

segments.name: Blueloop (mono-material sustainable packaging)
segments.commentary: Blueloop share of output is below 30% of material volume, up from the prior quarter; the balance of blueloop asset output (>70%) is used for products previously outsourced.

guidance_outlook: No numeric guidance given; management declined to commit to a quarterly EBITDA margin (said it could be 8%, 10% or 15%).
Management would not commit to INR750 crore quarterly revenue run-rate; said it depends on pass-through (single-digit), product mix and customer growth.
Volume growth expected to track market growth (about 4-5%); management said 23% growth should not be expected every quarter.
Festive season expected to support demand in coming months; inventory build-up at customers to be clearer by Q3 CY26 call.
Solar captive plant expected to come online in Q3 and supply ~50% of power for Khopoli plant.
capex_capacity: Volume growth was high single-digit (just short of double digit per management); exact capacity utilisation not disclosed on competitive grounds.
Productivity improvement programme over last 3-4 quarters is said to free capacity enough for growth; management sees no capacity constraint for at least a couple of years.
Modernisation and productivity capex funded from cash on balance sheet; no specific capex amount disclosed.
Solar captive power plant at Khopoli to be commissioned in Q3 CY26, supplying ~50% of Khopoli plant power.
Zero liquid discharge maintained; Taloja implemented mechanical vapour recompression water recycling.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in Q2 described as high single-digit; price, volume and mix each contributed roughly one-third of the 23% sales growth.
Raw material cost pass-through is contract-dependent (quarterly or monthly indexation, or ad hoc); management says most price changes occurred in Q2 and the process is 'never a done story'.
Customers valued supply reliability and contingency during the Middle East crisis; management said this drove share-of-wallet gains with same customer base.
Customer inventory build-up in anticipation of price increases is a tailwind; quantum not known to management.
Home care and liquid categories growing faster than food and beverage in India; late monsoon boosted beverage season.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q2 volume growth and export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was high single-digit, just short of double digit; exports and domestic grew at almost identical rates of about 23%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company pursuing volume growth again after sacrificing volume for profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not moved away from profitable growth; product mix and customer base have largely settled and the focus is share-of-wallet and innovation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR750 crore quarterly revenue run-rate reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit; INR750 crore includes single-digit price pass-through, and outcome depends on product mix and customer growth. It could be INR650 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is working capital and receivables trend (inventory and receivables roughly doubled; receivables ~50% of six-month turnover)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute values are higher due to price increases and higher volume; DSO and DIO are stable, and there are no realisation or ageing challenges.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for acquisitions or monetising land such as Daman?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific non-organic plans disclosed; cash is directed to modernisation and capex. Thane land sale was completed a couple of years ago; other land monetisation will be disclosed in annual reports if it happens.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth rate be sustainable into next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to track market growth (around 3-5%) rather than repeat 23% every quarter.

risks_watch: Customer inventory build-up may reverse, reducing volumes in coming quarters; management will update in Q3.
Raw material volatility from the Middle East crisis; pass-through lags and inventory cost effects on margins.
Working capital: inventory and receivables rose in absolute terms; DIO and DSO said to be stable, to watch next quarter.
Export duty and import tariff regulation uncertainty affecting export growth.
One-time INR8.8 crore prior-period depreciation charge in Q1 affecting reported EBIT; the Q2 and H1 comparison base.
summary.management_tone: Confident on results and strategy, citing profitable growth, and cautious on forward numbers, repeatedly declining to quantify volume, margin or revenue run-rate beyond the current quarter. Several answers on inventory build-up, pricing sustainability and acquisitions were deferred to the Q3 call or left undisclosed.
key_quotes: So what that means is we are selective on where we operate. We're selective on which customers we want to grow with.
We don't want to just take volume just for the sake of it, right? It doesn't deliver volume. If it doesn't deliver profit and return on investment, there's no point in doing that.
I would not worry about capacity utilization or amount of growth we can do at least for another couple of years.
